sentences.text:
For Appellants : Shri Rishikant Mahobia, Advocate For Respondent No. 3 : Shri Shivendu Pandya,
Advocate Hon'ble Shri Justice Sachin Singh Rajput Order On Board 19/09/2023 1.

This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1980 (for short 'the Act of 1980') has been filed by the appellants challenging the award dated 20/10/2016 passed in Motor Accident Claim case No.39/2014 by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (for short 'learned Tribunal'), Jashpur.
2.
The appellants / claimants have filed an application under Section 166 of the Act of 1988 on account of death of Pardeshi Tandon in an accident which took place on 06/07/2014.
As per pleadings of the claim application, the deceased along with three other persons on a motor cycle was coming towards village - Budhadhhand.

As they reached near a culvert, a Hyva truck bearing registration no.CG 14 D-1600 driven rashly and negligently by respondent No.2 / driver from the opposite side, dashed the motor cycle resulting into death of Pardeshi Tandon, Santosh and Ramesh Tandon and causing injuries to Govind Tandon.

As per further pleadings, deceased - Pardeshi Ram was aged about 30 years, he was working as a Carpenter in Jagdamba Glass Plywood and Sanitary Centre, Patthalgaon and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.

entities.text: Jagdamba Glass Plywood and Sanitary Centre
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The appellants / claimants claimed Rs.42,25,000/- as total compensation.
Respondents 1 and 2 filed their written statement and denied pleadings and pleaded that on the motor cycle, 3 to 4 persons were sitting, therefore, it is a case of contributory negligence.
Respondent No.3 / Insurance Company also filed written statement and denied the claim of the claimants.

Rest of the respondents have also denied the averments of claim application.
3.
On the basis of above pleadings, learned Tribunal framed as many as six issues.
The issue with regard to rash and negligent driving by respondent No.2 / driver of the offending vehicle was proved.
The issue with regard to violation of the insurance policy with regard to offending vehicle was held not proved.
With regard to issue of contributory negligence, it was held to be partly proved.

The issue with regard to violation of the conditions of the insurance policy of the motor cycle was held to be proved and as far as issues No.5 and 6 relief and cost are concerned, Rs.7,46,200/- was awarded in favour of the appellants / claimants and 70% of the said amount was to be paid by respondents 1 to 3 and 30% was to be paid by respondent No.4.
4.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the learned Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased as Rs.4200/- which is on the lower side as he was a skilled labour and working as Carpenter and looking to the evidence on record, the income ought to have been taken as Rs.15,000/-
per month.
He further submits that the finding with regard to contributory negligence is also incorrect because admittedly, the deceased was not driving the motor cycle and it was being rode by one Santosh.

Therefore, the question of contributory negligence does not arise and it is a case of composite negligence and the entire amount ought to have been directed to be recovered from respondent No.3 / Insurance Company.
No future prospect has been awarded and the compensation amount awarded under the other heads is also on the lower side.

2 5.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for respondent No.3 opposes the submission and submits that learned Tribunal has rightly assessed the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.4200/- and no income was proved by the appellants / claimants.
The finding with regard to contributory negligence does not require any interference because the appellants / claimants can recover the remaining amount from respondent No.4.
Therefore, no interference is called for.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties, considered their rival submissions and also perused the records.
7. The date of incident is 06/07/2014.
Learned Tribunal has considered the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.4200/-.

Looking to the evidence available on record, prevailing minimum wages and nature of job in which the deceased was engaged with, this Court has no hesitation to hold that the monthly income ought to have been considered as Rs.6,000/-.
Looking to the age, 40% future prospects ought to have been added.

Therefore, it would be appropriate to modify the assessment of compensation in the light of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Sarla Verma and ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation and ors., (2009) 6 SCC 121, National Insurance Co.
Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi and ors, (2017) 16 SCC 680 and Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and ors, (2018) 18 SCC 130.

sentences.text:
8. Learned Tribunal has awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.7,46,200/-
which is subtracted and enhanced compensation comes to Rs.7,28,800/-.
9.

Now the question arises whether the finding recorded by the learned Tribunal with regard to contributory negligence is required to be interfered with or not.?
10.
Counsel for the parties submit that the motor cycle on which the deceased was seated was rode by one Santosh which was hit from the opposite direction by the offending vehicle.
In view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of T.O.Anthony v. Karvarnan and ors, (2008) 3 SCC 748, the finding so recorded is absolutely incorrect.

entities.text: T.O.Anthony v. Karvarnan and ors, (2008) 3 SCC 748
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, that finding is set aside.

The entire amount of compensation shall be paid by the insurance company / respondent No.3 jointly and severally with respondents 1 and 2 within a period of 60 days @ 6% from the date of claim application.
11. Learned Tribunal will disburse the amount of compensation in terms of the award dated 20/10/2016.
The appeal, thus, partly allowed.
